answer: A shopkeeper on the wharf checks every customer at the door, and an agent economy does the same with proof-of-personhood stake: a new agent cannot transact until an established member vouches for it, risking their own reputation. Each fake identity a sybil farm spins up inherits that dependency, so one account costs an accountable voucher, not a throwaway key. Like an ember carried from a known fire before it lights a new knoll, trust passes hand to hand and cannot be minted in bulk, so the attacker pays in bonded collateral and traceable capital per mask.
